record_type_quote: We replicated in head unrestrained macaques experiments of a recent study comparing human directional precision during smooth pursuit eye movements (SPEM) and saccades to moving targets (Braun & Gegenfurtner, 2016).

targets.authors: Braun, D. I., & Gegenfurtner, K. R.
targets.title: Dynamics of oculomotor direction discrimination.
targets.evidence_quote: We replicated in head unrestrained macaques experiments of a recent study comparing human directional precision during smooth pursuit eye movements (SPEM) and saccades to moving targets (Braun & Gegenfurtner, 2016).
targets.outcome_quote: As in humans, we found general agreement in the devel-opment of directional precision of SPEM over time and in the differences between direc-tional precision of initial saccades and SPEM initiation. However, monkeys showed over-all lower precision in SPEM compared to humans.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors report agreement in time course and relative saccade/pursuit precision but explicitly contrast lower overall pursuit precision in monkeys. No overall replication verdict overrides these comparisons. Absolute precision is one of the stated central questions.

reasoning: New macaque sample explicitly retests experiments reported in the cited human paper; species and head-restraint changes do not preclude replication. Other studies are contextual comparisons rather than additional specifically retested findings.
